title: Slope: the steepness of a line

slides.title: How steep is the wire?
slides.text: Tally is stringing wires between the sky islands. One wire climbs 6 squares while it crosses 4, and another climbs only 3 while it crosses 6. Before anyone rides them, Tally wants one number that says how steep each wire is.

slides.title: Slope is up over across
slides.text: The slope of a line is how far it goes up for each step across. From A (0, 0) to B (4, 6) the line rises 6 while it runs 4, so its slope is 6/4, which is 3/2. Each single step across lifts the line by 1.5.

visual.label: A line from A to B with its rise and run

focus.cue: Start at A and end at B, two points on the line.
The run is 4 across and the rise is 6 up.
Rise over run: 6/4 = 3/2, the slope of the whole line.

slides.title: Any two points give the same slope
slides.text: Choose any two points on a straight line and the slope comes out the same. A small stair of 1 up for 2 across and a big stair of 3 up for 6 across have the same shape. So 1/2 and 3/6 are equal, and the line has one slope.

visual.label: A small stair and a big stair under one line

focus.cue: The small stair: 2 across, then 1 up.
The big stair: 6 across, then 3 up.
Both stairs fit the same line: 1/2 = 3/6.

slides.title: A line that goes down
slides.text: A line that falls from left to right has a negative slope. From (−4, 3) to (2, −3) it drops 6 while it runs 6 across. Subtract in the same order on the top and on the bottom, and keep the sign.

slides.title: A steady rate is a slope
slides.text: A cable car that climbs 2 meters every 4 seconds moves at a steady rate. Its graph is a straight line through (0, 0), and the slope of that line is the unit rate: 2/4 = 0.5 meters each second. A steeper line means a faster car.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.text: Four words for the steepness of a line.

words.means: how steep a line is: the rise divided by the run
how far a line goes up (or down) between two of its points
how far a line goes across between the same two points
how much of one quantity there is for each 1 of another

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Sky Lines at How Steep. Set the steepness of each wire, run it and see where it really goes. Then compare two steady rates.
slides.alt: Sky Lines on a phone: a grid with island A at the start and island B higher up, and a stepper to set how steep the wire is.
